newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Netcomm makes loss, to restructure.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Netcomm makes loss, to restructure.

text.p: Modem manufacturer Netcomm Ltd said on Friday it made a net loss of A$2.73 million in the latest six months and had begun a comprehensive restructuring of its operations.
The company said the net loss in the six months to December 31, 1996, was based on a fall in sales to A$18.52 million from A$26.75 million a year ago.
Netcomm, which listed in late 1993, said the first half loss was dominated by a A$1.5 million loss from its modem division and a A$1.0 million loss from cable development operations.

It said the first stage of the restructuring was announced in October 1996 but the latest changes were more substantial and "primarily involve reorganising the core modem business for better focus and to immediately return it to profitability, thus enhancing its position as the leading modem company in Australia". The restructuring would consist of an estimated A$2.0 million one-off charge, including costs from the retrenchment of 50 employees.
The company said its new business direction included an examination of possible mergers or equity partnership with a local or overseas company.
"There are continuing discussions with local and international companies for a possible medium term business merger in order to maximise the value of Netcomm's market leading position," it said.
It also said it was in the process of outsourcing its manufacturing operations, which should lead to savings of A$1.9 million in fiscal 1998.

"Netcomm is well advanced in negotiations with two parties for a total outsourcing and sale of Netcomm's under-utilised manufacturing operations. A decision is expected to be made and actioned in the next 90 days."
Netcomm shares were one cent higher on Friday at 61 cents, only one cent off their 12-month low. The stock has a 12-month high of A$1.80.
